title: Entrepreneurship: Starting and Running a Small Business
scope_note: Course scope: general education for US learners, not legal, tax or financial advice. Rules, fees and platform policies change and vary by state and city; each lesson says what to check and where. All businesses and people in the questions are fictional unless a lesson names a real company.

ENT.CASE.01.title: Apply a documented early decision (learning a skill cheaply and starting with one small shop) to a new small business

ENT.CASE.02.title: Apply a documented early decision (solving a problem you have and checking that others share it) to a new business

ENT.CASE.03.title: Apply a documented test (selling before holding inventory) to a new product idea, and see its limits

ENT.CASE.04.title: Apply a documented test (a demo with a sign-up list) and tell sign-ups from paying customers

ENT.CUST.01.title: Identify a specific, frequent problem that someone already spends time or money on

ENT.CUST.02.title: Describe a specific customer group instead of "everyone"

ENT.CUST.03.title: Write an offer (value proposition) that says who it is for, the problem and the result

ENT.CUST.04.title: Tell the paying customer from the user and the decision-maker

ENT.LEGAL.01.title: Tell a business name, a legal entity and a brand apart

ENT.LEGAL.02.title: Explain that a free domain or state name approval does not grant trademark rights, and what to check

ENT.LEGAL.03.title: Describe sole proprietorships and general partnerships, including personal responsibility for debts

ENT.LEGAL.04.title: Describe LLCs and corporations at a basic level, including what limited liability does and does not do

ENT.LEGAL.05.title: Separate an entity's legal form from how it is taxed

ENT.START.01.title: Describe a business as solving a problem for customers who pay, and tell revenue-seeking activity from a hobby

ENT.START.02.title: Compare a side business with a full-time business by time, income needs and risk

ENT.START.03.title: Classify a business idea as a service, physical product, digital product or content business, and name what each needs

ENT.TEST.01.title: Plan interview questions about what people already do rather than what they say they would do

ENT.TEST.02.title: Recognize and rewrite leading or yes-pushing interview questions

ENT.TEST.03.title: Identify direct competitors and the other ways customers solve the problem today

ENT.TEST.04.title: Choose a small, cheap test that answers one question about demand

ENT.TEST.05.title: Rank evidence of demand, with payments and pre-orders above opinions

ENT.TEST.06.title: Explain why likes, follows and compliments are weak demand signals

ENT.TEST.07.title: Decide from stated test results whether to continue, change or stop an idea
